📖 Baca

Bayern Munich stance on signing Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold 'revealed'

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (488 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32.
  • Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.
  • Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32.

Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.

Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.

The England international has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu under Jose Mourinho, with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries seemingly ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold was also subjected to boos from sections of the home support following his lacklustre performance in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo last week.

Former Liverpool and England striker Emile Heskey recently suggested that Alexander-Arnold should consider a move to Bayern, although he admitted he would love to see the defender return to Anfield.

However, Bild journalist Christian Falk has categorically dismissed the links, suggesting that Bayern are more interested in signing players such as Givairo Read than Alexander-Arnold.

Bayern already have Konrad Laimer and Josip Stanisic available for the right-back position, while Sacha Boey also remains at the club.

Even if Vincent Kompany decides to make changes in that department, he would reportedly favour a younger profile, meaning Alexander-Arnold is unlikely to be a genuine option for the German champions.

It has been revealed that speaking to CFBayern Insider, Falk said: "It is not true - Bayern Munich are interested in Real Madrid fullback Trent Alexander-Arnold. Bayern are searching for a player in this position, and players like Givairo Read are definitely still of interest.

According to recent reports, "You can tell from Read’s profile alone that the club just isn’t looking to add a player like Alexander-Arnold to the ranks. Also, I’m not sure if Vincent Kompany would look at the Englishman’s profile, as he’s not a typical right-back for Bayern Munich.

"He’s also not the youngest footballer any more. And, if we’re being honest, the 28-year-old hasn’t proven himself at Real Madrid.

Recent findings suggest that "You have to have a lot of respect for English players who give it a go playing in another country. But not every English player succeeds after leaving the UK, and not every English player is Harry Kane! So, I don’t think Alexander-Arnold will be a genuine option for Bayern in the summer.".

While an emotional return to Anfield would appeal to many supporters, the reality is that Liverpool have probably moved on, even though the right-back position remains a somewhat problematic area for them.

Jeremie Frimpong has yet to convince everyone, while there is also uncertainty over whether the Reds will sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a permanent deal.

With Conor Bradley's injury record remaining a concern and Joe Gomez potentially departing next summer, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in a new right-back, although it remains doubtful whether Liverpool would consider a move for their former player.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steven Pressley did not consider quitting in the wake of Dundee suffering their biggest-ever home defeat against Hearts on Saturday night.
  • According to recent reports, the 8-0 loss led the manager to take full blame afterwards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Pressley did not consider quitting in the wake of Dundee suffering their biggest-ever home defeat against Hearts on Saturday night.

According to recent reports, the 8-0 loss led the manager to take full blame afterwards. He stated he wanted to “crawl under a rock and hide” following such a landmark reversal.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that the 53-year-old has had little time to ponder his future. Dundee are back in action as soon as Tuesday night at Easter Road against Hibs, who are themselves hurting following a 4-0 home defeat against Dundee United in their last outing. "It has been a tough 24, 48 hours," stated Pressley. "There’s a lot of embarrassment, a lot of disappointment.".

It has been revealed that he stressed there was also a determination to learn from the most challenging experience of his managerial career. Although he has spoken before of coming close to walking away on at least two occasions last season, resigning had not crossed his mind this time.

“Not this weekend, no,” he said. “I've had to find strength from I don't know where, but not this weekend. Not this weekend. But it was hugely embarrassing.

“It probably ranks as the most embarrassing moment of my managerial career thus far.

“I'm 17, 18 years into my coaching career and it's why, in football, you can never become complacent.

“Because nothing ever surprises you. You think you've lived through everything, and then something else comes along. And very much that was Saturday.”.

Sources indicate that pressley has admitted considering quitting after disappointing results in his first season at Dundee, one of which was a 4-0 defeat at Pittodrie against Aberdeen. Dundee recovered from a poor start to the campaign and Pressley succeeded in getting his critics firmly on side.

Recent findings suggest that however, the historic nature of Saturday’s result meant he found himself under fire again from some quarters. Pressley has resolved to find the answers. Dundee will be without key defender Owen Bevan, who was sent off on Saturday night, against Hibs.

The club have decided against appealing the decision. “We accept the punishment,” said Pressley. “It is not ideal but I don’t think there was a real chance of it being overturned.”.

Pressley suggested there would not be a radical overhaul of the side or system. “It is difficult to change a lot in two days so we have to be very careful," he noted. "But we have thought a lot about what we can do. There has to be a change in (the suspended) Owen Bevan. There is a lot to consider. But the most vital thing is we give a response and try to get some level of pride back.”.

Sources indicate that buoyed by the permanent signing of winger George Vorster Hill played very well for 30 second-half minutes. Vorster put the visitors 2-1 in front on 75 minutes but then Hill seemed to go defensive and gave away a cheap free kick 25 yards out. Up stepped Fanimo to break away hearts.

Perhaps the more stinging result was a 1-0 home defeat to lowly Brentwood the previous Tuesday.

Industry observers note that mansell and his team held all the aces that night but for some reason couldn’t break out from a malaise. They produced one shot on target all evening. Away from first team matters we caught up junior section managers Tim Bourne and Ben Slade, who are passionate about providing a safe and nurturing environment for youngsters to play football.

As Tim explained: “We have over 500 players both training and playing matches across our three home facilities.”.

The MTC is a hive of activity on Saturday mornings for training and then the excellent latest facility The Arc and St Paul’s School host matches on Sundays.

Ben mentioned: “it’s a huge operation and while Tim and I are the face, there is a large committee of passionate people all performing different tasks, this wouldn’t function without them!.”.

In a recent development, hill’s Junior section has three teams at each age group, the youngest players are under-fives. They also facilitate coaching badges and referee courses. As Tim suggested: “It’s a well-oiled machine.”.

I ventured to the Arc last Sunday to catch up with the U13s girls team playing Fishersgate. It truly is a remarkable facility, a real mecca for youth football. Both teams put on a great performance as the visitors took a narrow victory.

The junior section is in rude health and going from strength to strength operating with the best facilities in Sussex.

Hill’s pathway section under Mansell and Berty Oliva are performing at an extraordinary level this season – the U18s and 19s Academy side continue to pick up great wins.

Striker Bobby Byrne – son of ex-Republic of Ireland, Brighton and QPR striker John Byrne – and is making all kinds of headlines after his nine goals in one U18 Sussex Cup match. He rapidly followed up with six for the U19s at Ebbsfleet.

After the six he explained: “It’s all going very well this season. I would like to take my football to the highest level I can but first would love to play for the Hillians.”.

Bobby’s name is on a lot of people’s lips right now – with many calling for him to make his first team debut. It’s a certainty we will be keeping an eye on his progress.

While the club are operating at a high level right now and are always looking to enhance the profile, the vast majority of fans and connections quite rightly engage only with first team matters.

Sources indicate that mansell is acutely aware of this so will be looking for a win when title contenders Eastbourne Borough travel to the MTC on Saturday afternoon. Three points at this time would be huge.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:42, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 13:43.

Barcelona will be without the services of Lamine Yamal for Wednesday's Champions League fixture with Sabah.

Yamal has been ruled out of the contest due to a minor ankle injury, with Barcelona not taking any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an issue that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was named on the bench and is likely to be brought back into the XI for this contest.

Fermin Lopez is facing a domestic suspension following his red card against Villarreal, so it is likely that there will be a start for the Spain international here.

Anthony Gordon is also in line to return to the XI, with Karim Adeyemi potentially moving across to the right due to Yamal's absence.

Gerard Martin and Joao Cancelo are both expected to feature at the back, while Eric Garcia is likely to continue at right-back despite the return to fitness of Jules Kounde.

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon.

Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

Recent findings suggest that this was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”.

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”.

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding fresh ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

It has been revealed that how different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

Sources indicate that neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0.

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

Chelsea break the deadlock inside a minute of the second half! ⚡ Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/E63rtGQnbv.

In a recent development, that should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

According to recent reports, he signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

Recent findings suggest that bizarrely, Alonso had as much cause to curse Tierney for the first of several contentious decisions, booking Armstrong for an aggressive but ultimately fair lunging challenge on Josh Acheampong. That enraged the home supporters to inspire Everton to their most dangerous spell, Thierno Barry coming closest to troubling Martínez before half-time.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Sources indicate that rogers’s reprieve changed all that. Inexplicably inconsistent as Tierney was, Chelsea exhibited a steel which thrilled Alonso as much as those games when Cole Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are in full flow.

“They didn’t score, but did a fantastic job for the team,” Alonso pointedly said of his attackers.

Alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s new home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

Thanks for reading along this afternoon.

A good win for Chelsea at Everton, but above all, let’s hope Martinez is back to full health soon.

Moyes accepted that his side had were not good enough.

He told TNT Sports: “We were a little bit unlucky with the goals. It wasn’t good defending, but it takes a couple of deflections before it gets to Neto. It makes it a relatively easy finish for him.

“The second one was a free-kick which obviously ricochets around, so I think there were parts of the game we did OK, but we didn’t offer enough to create enough, to make enough chances. I can’t think of many, so that is probably the biggest indictment.”.

He had a minor gripe over a first-half tackle that was reviewed, saying, “I think the Morgan Rogers tackle on Jimmy [Garner] could have been questioned.”.

However, given the good start to the season for Everton so far, he does not have too much rancour.

According to recent reports, on his first goal, he explained how Everton’s defensive approach allowed them to react: “We know that they came man-to man. In the second half we adjusted some stuff. We tried to get the best of the man-to-man press and we got away. We got the cross and I could finish well, so really happy.”.

He credited his Portugal coach, Jorge Jesus, with his calmness in front of goal, adding: “This comes a little bit from the new coach of the national team that claims when you are near to the area you need to pass to the goal, so really happy with that.”.

With Chelsea now in the Champions League places, Neto was keen to keep up the momentum. He said: “It’s really important. We know it’s tough to play away, even at home there are no easy games. We came here with personality, with good intentions to win the match and really happy with the result.”.

Chelsea captain Reece James’ surgery could be out for a couple of months, Xabi Alonso explained.

He told the  press: “I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks. It’s not going to be short. Whether it’s before or after Christmas then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.”.

It has been revealed that he is looking to vice captains Moises Caceido and Levi Colwill to step up in his absence, explaining: “You can be a captain without an armband, for sure. Leadership is important and that’s why we have this group, not just on matchday.”.

James remains vital to Chelsea at their best, and while his minutes have been managed, it’s a huge disappointment to see him need to go under the knife once more.

It has been revealed that in his press conference ahead of the weekend, Everton boss David Moyes was not too concerned by his relatively small squad.He said:  “Leicester City won the league with not too many players. We have not got too many players. I am not saying we’re going to win the league, but we want to try to challenge and be around the top teams.”.

That might be made harder by the news that the Friedkin Group are already looking to sell the club after only a couple of years in charge. Moyes is a rare thing, a manager who keeps improving despite setbacks, and his second spell has been fairly solid so far.

Moyes is aware that Chelsea pose a threat up front, adding: “Their attacking line is incredibly exciting. I also think they have got some super defenders as well, but they are playing quite an expansive game, which on its day can lead to goals and on another day it can lead to defeats.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

Yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

Recent findings suggest that next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

According to recent reports, david Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

That’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to initiative.

It’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

McInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for important goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

According to recent reports, not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

First in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

According to recent reports, both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

Sources indicate that particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

His sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

It has been revealed that that’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Recent findings suggest that fernandez announced himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

Sources indicate that A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He showed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

It has been revealed that in his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

Sources indicate that he put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

McInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

Breaking: Did ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe really need eye surgery after staring at solar eclipse?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.
  • Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.
  • A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, revealed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, revealed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour rapidly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’.

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

And the 67-year-old marked his appointment with a crucial victory over Fleetwood Town at the Broadfield Stadium on Saturday (November 21) – the Reds’ first win at home since March.

Blackwell and Warnock go way back, having coached alongside each other at a number of EFL clubs.

With the Reds travelling to Exeter City on Saturday (November 28), Blackwell was asked if he thought Warnock might be in the crowd.

It has been revealed that “I speak to Neil regularly,” the Reds boss mentioned. “We've been together for nearly 35 years, player and coach. So, we have a good chat.

“Myself and Neil have ended up, [for] the last seven or eight years, firefighting at Cardiff [City], at Rotherham [United], at Middlesbrough, where we've gone into this situation that we're in now, so we have a good idea.

Before that trip to Exeter on Saturday, the Reds welcome high-flying Barnet to the Broadfield Stadium on Tuesday night (November 24).

Blackwell’s side remain bottom of League Two and three points adrift of safety but have at least two games in hand on many of their closest rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It wasn’t quite the morning after the night before. Nevertheless, Dundee players were very obviously still bearing the mental scars on Monday nearly 48 hours after a night of infamy inflicted by Hearts.

An old adage is that it’s best to go again as quickly as possible to get the performance and - most urgently of all – the result out of the system.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“To a point, yes…” agreed Steven Pressley when this theory was put to him at the sun-sprayed Dundee training facility at Gardyne College Campus ahead of Tuesday’s return to action against Hibs.

According to recent reports, the counter argument, one the Dundee manager was clearly conscious of, is that three nights later is maybe just a bit too soon. In addition, when it comes to grounds Dundee might choose to visit for their next assignment after losing 8-0 – or should that be 0-8 – then Easter Road would not be high on the list. Dundee have not won there for a quarter of a century. The record books are being well-thumbed just now.

Industry observers note that “We obviously don’t have a lot of time to work on elements of our game blueprint,” said Pressley. “It has been pretty frantic.

“Not only have we had to blueprint how we have to play and be prepared for Hibernian, I have also had to think a lot about the management of the group and everybody within that. I have had to find a way to stabilise the group.”.

The employment of such words as “stabilise” reflect the harrowing nature of the experience. A group of 16 players including substitutes, many of them in their early 20s, endured something akin to a medical procedure.

Industry observers note that A rampant Hearts side removed their sense of self-belief with almost surgical precision. Professional sport is often about how rapidly such wounds can heal.

But this is upcoming territory for everyone, including those as steeped in the game as Pressley. Owen Goodman, the 22-year-old keeper on loan from Crystal Palace, was perhaps left with most to feel sore about on Saturday night as goal after goal whizzed past him.

Dundee presumably have a duty of care towards him. It’s maybe one reason why Pressley decided against showing a re-run of the match the following morning. “I didn’t think putting them through the agony of watching it again was helpful,” he remarked.

Goodman was the last Dundee player to leave the field and one of the first in on Monday. He mentioned never having let in eight goals before, even in academy games. This was new territory for so many.

Young men such as Goodman carry a huge burden of responsibility as they attempt to bounce back from a historic defeat. An updated edition of the definitive Dundee FC history book, They Wore the Dark Blue, has just been published. It’s already out of date in one respect. Although it contains every result, competitive and otherwise, dating back to 1893, the Dundee fans' bible doesn’t include what now stands as the club’s biggest-ever home loss.

Such landmark results usually belong in the late 1800s, rendered a curiosity rather than a wounding detail due to the passage of time.

In Dundee’s case, prior to Saturday, their biggest-ever home defeat was relatively recent – 1971, against a Celtic side who had been crowned European champions in recent enough memory for one newspaper to describe them having “conjured the magic of Lisbon” at Dens Park following their 8-1 win.

It has been revealed that aberdeen equalled the margin of victory if not the scoreline in 2017. But Hearts outdid both those results on Saturday night. When Stuart Findlay rose like Alan Gilzean to nod in No 8 with a minute or so of the game left, the old pillars in the Dens Park main stand might have warped a fraction in recognition of the goal’s significance. Even if few, least of all Findlay, were probably aware of it at the time. A historic low dating back to 1893 – 1899 in the case of Dens Park itself – had been recorded.

Extraordinary, unthinkable results do happen. Just ask Hearts. Five goals down to Falkirk at home just a few weeks ago, they at least rallied to 5-2. Rallying was something Dundee conspicuously failed to do, which might have been the most disappointing aspect of the night for Pressley personally. He shouldered the blame himself, citing his suspicion that a poor performance had been in the post. He just didn't realise how poor. When he sought to rectify things at half time by sending on three substitutes there was precious little reaction. If anything things got worse, with Dundee reduced to ten men due to Owen Bevan’s red card.

Often teams who rack up handsome half-time leads cannot maintain such intensity in the second half due to a combination of factors, including stiff resolve from the opposition to avoid further embarrassment. This wasn’t evident on Saturday. Hearts scored another four goals to match their first-half quota and might have scored more, with another chalked off for a handball.

Although he says he did not consider tendering his resignation, it’s safe to assume Pressley endured a long dark night of the soul on Saturday night when he returned home to Edinburgh.

Sources indicate that he said he found strength “from I don’t know where” and has been buoyed from a raft of messages of support. Perhaps Drey Wright, the Dundee wing-back, got to the heart of what it all meant on a human level.

“My six-year-old was at home watching the game, getting very upset with every goal that's going in,” noted the 30-year-old.

“My eight-year-old is putting his hand on the shoulder of my wife, kind of subconsciously helping her out. So that's not easy to hear.

Recent findings suggest that “I was back in training yesterday and later I was at the dinner table and my eldest indicates: ‘So Dad, what about that score last night?’ And it’s this kind of a back-to-reality moment. There’s no getting away from it.”.

  • Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a latest contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.
  • The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 13:45.

Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a latest contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.

Mac Allister revealed in September that Liverpool were not in a position to offer him a new contract, after the 27-year-old experienced a noticeable decline in individual performance levels in 2025-26.

However, after a positive World Cup with Argentina, Mac Allister has returned to form for Liverpool, scoring five goals and providing one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions so far this season.

The midfielder has started nine of Liverpool's 11 Premier League games under Andoni Iraola and also performed well in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, creating two chances, completing 89% of his passes and winning four of his five ground duels.

Nevertheless, ex-Liverpool midfielder Hamann does not believe that talks over a upcoming deal will begin for another three months, and any extension is only likely to be two years at best.

"They mentioned to him there's no contract now, and he's in his late 20s," Hamann told Sports Mole when asked if Mac Allister had already played his way into a fresh contract.

"If he carries on performing, if he keeps on scoring goals, then come February, March, April, there might be a time where you say. 'maybe we keep him another two years.' But I don't think there's any rush at the moment.".

Mac Allister - who turns 28 on December 24 - has come up with 24 goals and 21 assists in 167 matches for Liverpool since 2023, and he earns £180,000 a week under his current contract terms, according to Capology.

The Argentine's reported salary only makes him the 11th highest-paid player at Liverpool, below latest signing Ronald Araujo (£210k) and almost half of what Virgil van Dijk earns (£350k).

Mac Allister's relationship with Ryan Gravenberch blossomed to the maximum in the 2024-25 season, culminating in both midfielders becoming Premier League champions for the first time.

However, Mac Allister's decline from a defensive and box-to-box standpoint was striking; compared to 2024-25, he made 45% fewer tackles and 26% fewer recoveries than in the 2025-26 campaign.

Gravenberch's own form did not help the South American's cause, though, and the latter has had a rejuvenated look about him since the World Cup, immediately earning Iraola's trust in the process.

Mac Allister's availability remains exceptional too, as he has only missed 11 matches for club and country since joining Liverpool and has been involved in every match so far this season.

With Wataru Endo almost certainly on the way out and James McConnell still on the fringes, Liverpool should speed up the process of tying down Mac Allister, lest they risk losing another midfield option in 2027.

Didi Hamann was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Lottoland Live Casino.

The visitors best chance of the half came five minutes before the break when Sam Pidgeon worked his way to the edge of the Heath penalty area and hit a left foot shot which deflected off the Heath goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield and flew narrowly wide of the post – but it remained 1-0 a the break.

The Us started the second half well, forcing Heath on to the backfoot but failing to create any clear-cut chances.

Their most dangerous tactic seemed to be launching long throws into the Bears penalty area where they met by a solid-looking Broadbridge Heath defence marshalled by Lewis Hyde and supported by his protégé Jay Richardson.

But the Bears doubled their lead on the hour mark when Young received the ball wide on the right of the Hastings penalty area and forced his way forward, where he was challenged by a defender – bringing the Heath player crashing to the ground.

The match referee had no doubt about it being a foul, pointing immediately to the penalty spot, and MoM Young picked himself up, dusted himself down and hammered the spot kick into the back of the net for his second of the afternoon, helping his side to a 2-0 win.

The victory saw Broadbridge Heath move into one of the play-off places in seventh – just one point behind Hastings United.

Fixtures continue to come thick and fast with the Bears travelling to second-placed Erith Town on Tuesday evening before returning home again on Saturday to face leaders Faversham Town.

Martin O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is back to his very best and harbours no fears about the defender’s fitness levels ahead of a frantic festive schedule.

Although the Celtic manager substituted Tierney towards the end of Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren, the player started – and finished – both of Scotland’s games in the recent international window, when he was deployed as left centre-half in a back-three formation favoured by new international manager Sebastien Pocognoli.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

O’Neill admits this could be an option for Celtic if he chooses to play a system that he once was synonymous with during his first spell in charge at the club.

According to recent reports, “Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it,” noted O’Neill. “He competes better in the air than I ever thought he did.

It has been revealed that “It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that. He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.”.

Industry observers note that celtic face a tough upcoming run of games, including travelling to take on second-tier Portuguese club Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night. Two more away games against Hearts and Dundee promptly follow. The Parkhead side have just one more home match – against St Johnstone – before Christmas. Two other assignments, against Aberdeen and Omonia Nicosia, are away.

O’Neill has already spoken of “manoeuvring” players in the first-team squad to ensure no one is pushed beyond their limits.

Industry observers note that tierney clearly merits the most concern given his injury history. However, he has been quietly putting in the minutes for his club as well as his country in recent weeks. He has played the full 90 minutes of two of Celtic’s last four matches and was only subbed off on Saturday with 20 minutes left against St Mirren with the game already won. O’Neill revealed that he has a crafty tactic for dealing with the player if he begins to look like he might want to come off; he pretends not to notice him. There is no point in the player looking forlornly towards the dugout.

“Tierney played two 90 minutes for Scotland and that made it difficult for him to last the full game against St Mirren,” mentioned O'Neill.

In a recent development, “Internationals take it out of you and he played every second. He played left centre back and that maybe means less running, but those games are tough.

“Previous to his injury, he was feeling it. But since he’s been back, he’s played a lot of games. Sometimes with Kieran, when you feel as if he’s flagging, you just ignore him. If he’s coming near you, you turn away because you want him to play the games!

“Kieran has done great for me,” he added. "He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too. Kieran will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that “Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal. He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too.

In a recent development, “I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about Kieran. He’s a great lad too - very popular in the dressing room.”.

Alfred Johansson insists Motherwell’s latest accounts show the club are trending upwards - with Norway’s Bodo Glimt a key reference point.

Industry observers note that the Premiership side have reported a profit of £2.3M, which rises to £3.1M when excluding depreciation and finance costs, for the 2025/26 financial year. A record of £5M was generated from player trading while former manager Jens Berthel Askou achieved a fourth place finish in last term’s top flight.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that current manager Johansson’s work was largely in Scandinavia before travelling to Motherwell. He watched Bodo’s rise from lowly divisions to Champions League competitors and feels that shows what a step-by-step approach can do for a club’s long term aspirations. Former Rosenborg gaffer Johansson noted: “I can't really use that to ask for more time in terms of performing but definitely, it's evidence of what the club has been doing for the past 18 months at least, that it’s something that is working.

It has been revealed that “So that alignment in the club, that philosophy, and that strategy, like we do things like this, and the connection I feel between people inside here and the offices, that everyone wants to pull together in that direction. That is what gives you output all the time.

It has been revealed that “This is a club that the budget is very small compared with some of the teams that we want to compete with. That was the same for Bodo/Glimt 10 years ago. Their budget was so small, they went down to the 2nd division in Norway, now they are playing Champions League. You have to build stone by stone, and that's what Motherwell are trying to do, and that's what I feel every day inside these walls.”.

Industry observers note that motherwell’s long-term goals are also set to be boosted by a training base being built at nearby Dalziel Park where they right now undergo preparation for matches. Johansson is keen to see the club build on its ability to grasp marginal gains. He explained: ”You don't have that much time in football nowadays. I get asked in the press conference about patience and everything is related to time.

Sources indicate that “That means that you have to make the most out of your time. Maybe before 30 years ago you had to optimise every week. Now you have to optimise every hour in top football. That's down to recovery of players, work with their bodies, and you need facilities to be able to facilitate that work. So that's one part of it.

“That you need to add the facilities for the players to be able to do the work that's needed to play every few days and with that intensity that. Now I saw that from all the top leagues in Europe, that the Scottish Premiership was the second in the world in explosive accelerations, for instance.

“That's one of the more demanding things that you can put the body through. So you need to be able to react. You need to recover from that between matches and trainings, and so on. So you need the facilities for that. We don't have that much time. Right now we are driving back and forth to Dalziel Park. I could maybe take five minutes in my office with a player or on the pitch talking to a player. All of this is optimising time and I think it's essential today.”.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley spoke last week of the lack of national performance centre in Scotland, like Sweden are building in Johansson’s homeland. He added: “I definitely see the point of that's needed. I mean, Denmark, they've been working also now for some years.

Sources indicate that “They have a plan now in place for how to build that centre, Sweden the same. Uh, we know that other countries, they did it 20 years ago, like like the Belgians and the Portuguese FA, they did it. They built a new facility after the Euros. So, of course, it's there to push things and it's needed.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roffey faced clear table toppers Haywards Heath, at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on Saturday, determined to gain revenge for the narrow, and perhaps undeserved, loss at Hanbury Park earlier in the season. However, in the end, despite having 14 attempts on goal with 6 on target, it was the visitors who took the points with two clinical finishes from their four on target efforts and two off target.

Sources indicate that in the second minute Jordan Mase went down the left then cut in and switched the ball across the box to Luke Harrison whose shot took a slight deflection, taking the pace off it and Ethan McGrath in the Blues goal saved. In the fourth minute Mase again advanced before squaring it, this time to Stan Berry who hit a fierce drive just past the right-hand post, with McGrath probably covering it. Two minutes later Tom Caplin fed Moyo on the right and after his first cross was blocked at the near post he found Caplin 12 yards out but his shot although right in the corner, lacked the pace to beat McGrath.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Boars continued to dominate possession and after a quarter of an hour, Mase set the ball back for Charlie Gibson to fire over from twenty yards. Next a Gibson corner was deflected up in the air by a defender and Pat Gibs headed it back into the danger area where Berry controlled the ball in the air before hitting a spectacular bicycle shot a foot over the bar. Gibson hit his hot wide at the end of quick break and Berry hit the side netting after good work from Harrison and Callum Kilkenny.

In a recent development, heath had their first attempt on goal after twenty-two minutes when Sonny Causton was played through, but with defenders converging, hit his shot from the edge of the box straight at Charlie Burton. Back came Roffey and Teddy Wood put a twenty yarder narrowly past the right-hand post. Heath responded with Mark Goldson getting behind the defence, but Pat Gibbs held him up and the Boars got men back with his attempt ending tamely in Burton’s arms. Goldson had another chance when the ball was switched from the right, but he sliced his shot wide.

The breakthrough came on thirty-three minutes when a Roffey attack broke down, and the ball was quickly transferred to Josh Wright who had kept himself onside. Burton advanced to push him wide but Callum Kilkenny who had sprinted back went over the top of the outstretched keeper and Wright managed to squeeze the ball in at the far post despite the desperate efforts of Jack Meeres on the line. Wood replied with a shot that was saved comfortably by McGrath. After all that action the half ended quietly with the visitors having the advantage.

Roffey had the first attempt on goal after the break with Moyo’s shot being taken above his head by McGrath. The game became much more contained with Heath happy to close Roffey down and maintain their lead. The next significant action didn’t come until thirteen minutes before time when Roffey lost possession in their own area but forced Harry Shooman to shoot over. Roffey were still very much in the game, but this changed on eighty minutes as they threw men forward, the hosts were caught on the break and Wright held off Meeres and rolled the ball past Burton to double the lead. Roffey wouldn’t give up but Heath were now able to sit back and soak up the pressure. Gibsons free kick hit the wall and deflected for a corner which was cleared. As stoppage time approached the Boars had a great chance to stay in the game when Caplin spread the play out to Harrison whose cross picked out the same player, unmarked ten yards out, but he scuffed his shot and McGrath saved. There was still time for Moyo to force a save out of McGrath at the near post and the same player hit a shot wide but unfortunately time had run out for the Boars. The table toppers had shown a clinical edge and managed their way to the three points.

Roffey are still very much in the fight for a top five place and it looks like that could be between eight or nine teams and the Boars next match is away to one of them, Hassocks who sit two places above the Boars, on December 1st.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs(Moyo), Meeres, Wood, Mase, Berry(Allen), Caplin, Kilkenny(Hoarty). Subs: Pearse, Skerry.

Man Utd make decision on what to do next after Leny Yoro's controversial red card against Liverpool

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (394 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:57, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 14:51.
  • Manchester United have reportedly notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card.
  • The centre-back was sent off during Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday after bringing down Alexander Isak as the striker raced through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:57, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 14:51.

Manchester United have reportedly notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card.

The centre-back was sent off during Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday after bringing down Alexander Isak as the striker raced through on goal.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into the contest, a moment that significantly altered the complexion of the game as Liverpool enjoyed greater possession and created better opportunities.

While Man Utd could arguably have done more to frustrate the Reds, there is little doubt that Yoro's dismissal had a major bearing on the outcome.

According to Sky Sports, the Red Devils intend to appeal Yoro's dismissal, with Mauricio Pochettino offering his interpretation of the incident after the game.

The main point of contention is whether the foul constituted a clear denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with questions surrounding whether Isak was actually in control of the ball.

Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations when determining whether a player should be sent off for Denying an Obvious Goal-Scoring Opportunity (DOGSO) is whether the attacking player had control of the ball.

Pochettino not only questioned that aspect of the decision but also highlighted the referee's failure to penalise Jeremy Jacquet for his challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments earlier.

It remains to be seen how the FA will assess the incidents, although former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher has backed the on-field decisions in both cases.

Unless the decision is overturned following an appeal, Yoro is set to serve a one-match domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban, as his denial of a obvious goalscoring opportunity was a non-violent offence.

While the defender is available to face Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, he will miss Man United's next Premier League fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro will then be available to return to Premier League action on December 2 when Pochettino's side travel to St James' Park to take on Newcastle United.

The Red Devils are now without a win in their last nine Premier League matches and have slipped to 19th in the table, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

Celtic’s historic European dream hinges on remaining unbeaten in their next two Europa League ties in Portugal and Cyprus as they seek to build on the win over Besiktas before the international break.

Sources indicate that this, at least, is manager Martin O'Neill's view ahead of Thursday night's clash against Torreense, who have already amassed twice as many points as Celtic. The Portuguese second-tier side might be the most likely source of the win O'Neill feels is required. He has challenged his team to secure four points from the next two away fixtures.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that the 3-2 win over Besiktas earlier this month breathed some life back into the Parkhead club’s European campaign. "It gives us a chance, you know," said O'Neill.

Celtic are currently sitting 32nd out of 36 teams in the standings. They will have to break latest ground to finish among the top 24 and secure a place in the knockout stage. No team has managed to do so after opening with three defeats in the new European league format.

Sources indicate that after Torreense in Leiria on Thursday Celtic travel to meet Omonia Nicosia in their final European game before Christmas. They play Marseille and Union St. Gilloise early in the newly introduced year.

Sources indicate that “You'd have to think that we'd need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance so that you've got two left over, including a home game, which will not be easy," stated O'Neill. "It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

"We've taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so," he added. "It's the aim of the football club, it's what we've always said." O’Neill recalled a sponsors’ event last week where someone mentioned the manner of the Champions League qualifying exit. “Sometimes you feel as if we've never really got over the LASK thing,” he said.

Although much is at stake, O’Neill is still confident that bit-part players to date such as Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg can play a part in the European effort.

Both were signed on the last day of the summer transfer window and were included in the European squad. Sorensen has failed to make an impression despite starting the opening two Europa League defeats against Ferencvaros and Benfica while Van den Berg has been sidelined with an ankle injury.

Recent findings suggest that the Dutch midfielder made his belated debut as a substitute in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Sorensen, meanwhile, has not featured in the last two matchday squads due to a family bereavement. Celtic face a period where auxiliary players will be required to step up.

“This is a chance, with a bit of luck, for the likes of Sorensen and Van den Berg,” remarked O’Neill. He challenged Van den Berg to kick on following his cameo at the weekend. He hopes Sorensen, too, can begin to nail down a regular place in the side.

"He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,” said the manager “I think that he also arrived late as well too, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do.

"And whatever we do, I bet you it'll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma. But now it would be up to him.”.

According to recent reports, viljami Sinisalo has been waiting for his turn back in goal. O’Neill still hasn't made up mind about who will stay at No. 1.

Recent findings suggest that sam Johnstone is clearly in possession of the gloves at present even if it would not be a surprise if Sinisalo is given a match before long, perhaps as soon as Thursday. “There’s still good competition,” remarked the manager. “Viljami wants to be the keeper here, which is great.

Industry observers note that “He will play again and at some stage you have to make you’re mind up who will stay as no.1. I don’t think there’s a phenomenal amount between them at this stage.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.

Since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United. It was obvious from the moment they arrived at the Oval that they would only be happy with all three points, preferably by at least the same scoreline.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The early encounters went to United, and with just seven minutes on the clock James Jull shot home, only for the linesman to raise his flag for offside to howls of derision from the home support.

Guernsey started to make their mark with a couple of runs from Charlton Gauvain, but the visitors also left their mark on United’s players, collecting two yellow cards.

Hull went very close with an acrobatic scissor kick, and Joe Overy continued to needle away down the left wing, Charlie Ball forcing the keeper into a good save from one of Overy’s low crosses.

In first half added time, Guernsey took the lead with a fine shot from range beating Alieu Secka.

United were unperturbed and Rhyle Ovenden was unfortunate not to even it up straight after the break, his free kick just scraping the top of the crossbar.

On the hour Hull was replaced by Callum Barlow, before the increasingly confident Ovenden had a shot well saved by the Lions keeper.

According to recent reports, five minutes later, Barlow’s lightning-fast cross found Overy, who turned and slotted home well for 1-1. Overy rarely misses an attempt in the area, and Guernsey looked crestfallen.

There was a third and a fourth yellow card for Guernsey, who were pondering returning with only a point, when Ball broke past the defences and slotted home with an inch perfect side foot to make it 2-1 to United to the joy of the crowd, and despair of the islanders.

Rather than crumble, it galvanised Guernsey, and the United lead only lasted four minutes as Gauvain made it 2-2. Now it was a real blood and thunder contest, both teams showing exactly why they are in the top four, Secka made a wonderful save to keep it equal, Ball and Barlow both trying out the away keeper, but it remained 2-2.

After months out injured, the home crowd were delighted to see – on 85 minutes – Mason Creese come on, replacing Ball, and Freddie Jones took up position on the other flank replacing Overy.

Both added even more pace, and despite the cold, the crowd were heating up – while Guernsey overheated as they collected a fifth yellow in what was never a nasty encounter. As the final whistle went both teams were treated to an ovation as they left the field. This is the sort of fare non-league crowds absolutely love - hard tackling, fast attacking, stout defending and not a player from either side faking injury to get an opponent booked.

Both teams should be in the play-offs - one of them could be champions, time will tell.

Industry observers note that next up for United, this Saturday, is a home game with an improving Forest Row, who will be desperate for the points to help them out of the drop zone. It’s a 3pm kick-off at the Oval.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he mentioned, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

According to recent reports, 🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, it should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he said. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

According to recent reports, ‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

Sources indicate that ‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

Industry observers note that he added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

Raith Rovers have been charged by the Scottish Football Association over a social media post mocking Dunfermline Athletic manager Neil Lennon in the aftermath of the Fife derby.

Following the 0-0 draw at Stark's Park on November 6, Lennon made a pinching gesture with his thumb and forefinger towards rival supporters which was widely interpreted as a jibe calling Raith Rovers a "small club".

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Shortly after the final whistle, Raith's official X account shared a photo of Lennon making the gesture alongside the caption, "How big is your penis, Neil?". The club deleted the post 52 minutes later after it went viral.

The SFA compliance officer has now issued the Kirkcaldy outfit with a notice of complaint relating to a breach of Disciplinary Rule 73, which reads: "No recognised football body, club, official, Team Official or other member of Team Staff, player, match official or other person under the jurisdiction of the Scottish FA shall in an interview, a ‘blog’ on the internet, on a social networking or micro-blogging site, or in any other manner calculated or likely to lead to publicity, make comment(s) of a discriminatory or offensive nature based on, but not limited to, race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation or disability, or that endorse or encourage foul play or violent Conduct or are otherwise offensive.

"There shall be a presumption that any material published in such a manner was published in the name of and/or with the authority of the person or body bearing to have published the material.".

Sanctions typically start at a £500 lower-end fine and rise up to a £5,000 top-end fine.

Recent findings suggest that speaking about the incident last week, Lennon described the episode as "embarrassing for them", referring to Raith, adding; "“You know, that’s like an official club Twitter account, which is embarrassing. I’ll say no more than that.”.

In a recent development, raith are scheduled to face a Hampden disciplinary hearing on December 17. This falls just over a week before the two sides meet again at East End Park on Boxing Day.

Brighton were frustrated after failing to make their first-half dominance count, but midfielder Andres is looking ahead to the visit of Romanian league leaders Universitatea Craiova in the Uefa Conference League.

Sources indicate that “This is the Premier League, no? If you don't use the chances you have, and then you give this kind of team the opportunity to beat you, that is what they got.”.

Andres added that Albion must accept the defeat, learn from it and move forward swiftly.

Thursday's meeting with Craiova offers an immediate opportunity for Brighton to respond.

💡 Key Takeaways
